articles.title: "Putting her in this group is ridiculous": Outrage over Caitlin Clark's inclusion in 'Everybody Hates' show
articles.standfirst: VICE TV’s lineup has sparked immediate criticism over how the WNBA star is being framed
articles.summary: VICE TV’s lineup has sparked immediate criticism over how the WNBA star is being framed
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark ’s next major television appearance was supposed to examine the intense attention that has followed her rise through college basketball and into the WNBA . Instead, much of the early conversation has centered on the company she is keeping.

VICE TV’s upcoming six-part anthology series, Everybody Hates, will devote individual episodes to polarizing sports figures, with Clark joining a lineup that also includes Jake Paul, Aaron Rodgers, Michael Vick, Cristiano Ronaldo and Floyd Mayweather Jr .

The announcement immediately drew pushback from fans who argued that Clark ’s presence alongside several athletes associated with very different kinds of controversy creates an uncomfortable comparison.

“Caitlin Clark does not belong on the same list as these men,” one fan wrote. Another added: “Clark is hated for no reason, but she shouldn’t be here. I get why they likely chose her, but still.”

Fans question framing around Clark

The strongest reaction focused on whether Clark ’s polarizing status is comparable to the reputations of some of the other subjects.

“This is just not good company to be in and I am not even a fan of CC, but extremely odd to put her next to abusers in this,” one commenter wrote.

Another fan said: “So, the worst thing a woman can do is be passionate and competitive for her to be in the same lineup with these awful, disgusting men? Got it.”

WNBA analyst and CBS Sports sideline reporter Ashley Nicole Moss was similarly blunt. “Putting Caitlin Clark in this group is ridiculous,” Moss wrote.

Not every reaction rejected the premise entirely. One fan argued that the hostility surrounding Clark is often directed at the broader discourse around her rather than Clark herself.

“Everyone hates CC’s weird fans. I think there is significantly less hate for her personally,” the commenter said.

Focus on fame, scrutiny and public reaction

Clark ’s episode is scheduled for November 10 and is expected to examine how she became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball and the media storm that has followed.

Sports personality Rachel A. DeMita and journalist Jemele Hill are set to discuss Clark’s rise and the debate surrounding her public image. The series is scheduled to premiere Oct. 27 at 9 p.m. ET, with episodes also set to air through VICE TV’s YouTube channel.

Clark has appeared in a major docuseries before. ESPN+ featured her prominently in Full Court Press, which followed her final season at Iowa and transition toward the WNBA.

Clark’s profile continues to grow

The timing of the announcement comes as Clark is again dominating attention for her basketball.

She posted 27 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and four steals in Indiana’s 96-77 victory over Minnesota on Tuesday, then drew praise after giving her game-worn shoes to two young fans.

“CC, you’re just impressive… thank you for being a role model for our kids,” one fan wrote afterward.

That contrast is part of what has fueled the reaction to Everybody Hates. VICE’s premise may be about polarizing sports personalities.

Many fans, though, appear to believe Clark ’s inclusion says as much about the culture surrounding her as it does about the player herself.

articles.title: WNBA Playoff Picture 2026: Teams, standings, and bracket heading into the final day of the regular season
articles.standfirst: Minnesota locked into No.1, but Thursday will settle two key battles before playoffs begin
articles.summary: Minnesota locked into No.1, but Thursday will settle two key battles before playoffs begin
articles.body:
The WNBA reaches the final day of its regular season with the playoff field already locked, but the bracket is still not complete.

Minnesota has secured the No.1 seed, while Atlanta, Dallas and New York also know exactly where they will finish.

The remaining uncertainty centers on Golden State and Las Vegas in the race for second and third, along with Indiana and Washington in the battle for fifth and sixth.

That means Thursday’s results will determine two of the four first-round pairings before the playoffs begin Sunday.

Current WNBA standings entering final day

Minnesota sits at 32-11 and cannot be caught after clinching the top seed earlier in the week.

Golden State is 31-12, one game ahead of Las Vegas at 30-13. Atlanta is locked into fourth at 30-14 after beating New York , while Indiana enters Thursday at 28-15 and Washington follows at 27-16.

Dallas has secured seventh at 27-17, and New York is locked into eighth at 26-18.

Golden State Valkyries — 31-12

Washington Mystics — 27-16

What playoff bracket looks like right now

If the standings stay unchanged, the opening round would feature:

No.1 Minnesota Lynx vs. No.8 New York Liberty

No.2 Golden State Valkyries vs. No.7 Dallas Wings

No.3 Las Vegas Aces vs. No.6 Washington Mystics

No.4 Atlanta Dream vs. No.5 Indiana Fever

Minnesota and New York are already locked into their 1-versus-8 matchup, while Dallas will face whichever team finishes second between Golden State and Las Vegas .

Atlanta will meet the team that finishes fifth, meaning Indiana and Washington still have plenty at stake.

Minnesota enters postseason as top seed

The Lynx have spent most of the season near the top despite beginning the year without Napheesa Collier .

Rookie Olivia Miles has been central to that success, averaging 19.9 points and 6.1 assists while quickly establishing herself as one of the league’s most productive guards.

Las Vegas remains dangerous behind A’ja Wilson , while Golden State has built its season around defense and depth.

Indiana also enters the postseason with significant offensive firepower behind Kelsey Mitchell, Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston .

Tiebreakers could decide final order

The WNBA’s tiebreak system begins with head-to-head record.

If teams remain tied, the next criteria are winning percentage against teams finishing .500 or better, head-to-head point differential, point differential against .500-or-better opponents and overall point differential.

Those rules could still matter Thursday if the remaining contenders finish level.

Eight teams are already in. What remains is the final order, and with the playoffs beginning Sunday, there is almost no time between the last regular-season game and the start of the championship chase.

articles.title: Where to watch Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx? TV channel and schedule for Caitlin Clark’s last regular season game
articles.standfirst: Napheesa Collier's League-Best Lynx Host Caitlin Clark and the Fever at Target Center
articles.summary: Napheesa Collier's League-Best Lynx Host Caitlin Clark and the Fever at Target Center
articles.body:
T he last game of the season arrives at the Target Center with the WNBA's best regular-season team on one side and one of the sport's biggest draws on the other.

The Minnesota Lynx welcome the Indiana Fever to Minneapolis in a matchup that pits the No. 1 overall seed against a battle-hardened Eastern Conference qualifier — and reignites a rivalry that produced one of the summer's most memorable regular-season nights.

Schedule and Where to watch the Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx game

Tip-off for the Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx game is set for the evening of Thursday, September 24 at 8:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. Central Time and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time). The game will be played at the Target Center in Minneapolis, a building with a capacity of 19,356.

The WNBA coverage this season is carried across different networks, but for this particular game between Indiana and Minnesota, you’ll be able to watch it on USA Network and through streaming in YouTube TV, DIRECTV, or Sling TV.

Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx: Two teams arriving from very different places

Minnesota is finiching the regular season as the league's dominant force. The Lynx closed 32–10, the best record in the entire WNBA , and topped the Western Conference standings with a plus-315 point differential. That combination of scoring punch (3,834 points) and defensive discipline (3,519 allowed) is the profile of a genuine title favorite.

Indiana comes in as the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference at 27–15, and league-wide the Fever ranked fifth. Notably, no team in the WNBA scored more points across the regular season than Indiana's 4,060 — a testament to the firepower this roster brings into the playoffs. The Fever also owned a healthy plus-244 differential, so while the seeding gap is real, the offensive ceiling is not.

The two clubs are trending in opposite directions entering the series, however. Minnesota bounced back from a home loss to the New York Liberty with a 101–89 road win at the Connecticut Sun on September 20. Indiana, meanwhile, stumbled into the break, falling 93–77 at home to the Washington Mystics on that same date after a convincing win over Toronto two days earlier.

Both of these teams met in Minneapolis on August 2, and the Lynx handled business with a 108–100 win — the Fever's only prior trip to the Target Center this year. Minnesota's ability to hang triple digits on a good defensive night is exactly the kind of scoreboard pressure that can wear on a road team in a playoff environment. Indiana will need to be far more efficient defensively than it was in that August loss or in the recent defeat to Washington.

Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx: Key players and rosters

The Lynx are built around forward Napheesa Collier, the two-way engine who sets the tone at both ends and gives Minnesota a go-to scorer in the halfcourt when possessions tighten in the fourth quarter.

Around her, the Lynx have veteran guard play and shooting in Kayla McBride and Courtney Williams , with Natasha Howard providing frontcourt muscle and rebounding. Guard Olivia Miles adds youthful creativity to a backcourt that already has plenty of playoff-tested experience. It's a roster with balance — scoring from multiple positions and the kind of defensive versatility that produced the league's stingiest differential.

Indiana's identity starts with guard Caitlin Clark, whose passing range and deep shooting can flip a game in stretches and who will command Minnesota's full defensive attention. Alongside her, Kelsey Mitchell provides scoring bursts off the dribble, while center Aliyah Boston anchors the interior on both ends — her rebounding and rim presence will be crucial against Howard and Collier.

Wing depth from Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull gives Indiana perimeter defenders and outside shooting. This is a group that led the league in points for a reason: when the shots fall, the Fever can outscore anyone.

Prediction for the Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx game

Everything about the profile favors Minnesota — best record, best differential, home court, and a prior win over this exact opponent at this exact venue. Indiana's offensive ceiling makes an upset possible if Clark gets hot and Boston controls the paint, but the Lynx's two-way balance and Collier's presence in crunch time should carry the night. Expect a high-scoring, physical opener with Minnesota pulling away late — Lynx by 7 to 9 points.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham: "Call me Patrick Mahomes from now on"
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard responded on X to a video from the club in which she sends a ball into the second tier of the stands.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard responded on X to a video from the club in which she sends a ball into the second tier of the stands.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham wrote on Wednesday on X: "Call me Patrick Mahomes from now on," quoting the Fever’s post with a video of her throwing a ball to the second level of the stands at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. "Sophie Cunningham THREW this ball all the way to the second level," the team’s message said. Cunningham is an outspoken Kansas City Chiefs fan , Mahomes’s team, three-time Super Bowl champions.

The throw came after Indiana's 96-77 victory over the Minnesota Lynx on Tuesday, September 22. Cunningham played 29 minutes and scored 11 points.

Cunningham could be out of the league by 2027.

Sophie Cunningham has a new nickname, but also a question mark that could shape her future in the WNBA . The Indiana Fever player might not remain with the team next season and her future in the league could even be in doubt.

Analyst Robin Lundberg predicted that Cunningham will not be with the Fever next season and that she could be out of the WNBA. "If I had to predict it, Sophie Cunningham will not be with the Indiana Fever next year. And there is a possibility that she will not be in the league", he said. He acknowledged her performance, but added: "When you say that practices are too hard and then play seven minutes in the next game, people are going to say: "hmmm"".

'Sophie had spoken about the practices on her podcast "No Hesitation" , in an episode aired on September 17. "We keep practicing about two hours against the guys, going hard. And we still have four games left", Cunningham said. She also posed: "Why can't we do it in an hour and 20 or in an hour and 30? Why does it have to be two hours?". In the same episode she clarified that she likes to practice and that "everyone has their own style".'

Three days later, on Sunday, September 20, I ndiana Fever fell 93-77 to the Washington Mystics at home, in a game in which they underperformed.

The guard played seven minutes, missed both of her shots, did not record any stats, and finished with a Fever -11 , the worst mark on the team . Coach Stephanie White said after the game that "they needed some defensive help" and that they were looking for which group gave them the best option.

Against the Lynx , Cunningham played 29 minutes again. It was her best production in weeks and her biggest role in more than a month, according to Yardbarker. This season she is averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists in 22.7 minutes per game, all off the bench.

'Lundberg also referred to her activity off the court. "She is laying the groundwork for her post-playing career with the podcast. Obviously, she is extraordinarily popular and is very good at giving her unfiltered opinion. No team wants to be constantly talking about what one of its players said. Especially when she is a role player", he said. At the end of July, Cunningham signed with Groov, a custom template company, in a deal that includes an equity stake .'

The Fever (28-15) close the regular season this Thursday, September 24, in Minneapolis , once again against the Lynx. According to ClutchPoints, Indiana needs to win to secure fourth place and home-court advantage in the first round. The playoffs begin on Sunday, according to the Star Tribune.

articles.title: Angel Reese's coach explains what happened to her in the locker room after the hit from Sabrina Ionescu
articles.standfirst: Reese was cleared by medical staff, but the Dream chose not to risk its star forward before the playoffs
articles.summary: Reese was cleared by medical staff, but the Dream chose not to risk its star forward before the playoffs
articles.body:
Angel Reese’s status became an immediate concern Wednesday night after the Atlanta Dream forward took a blow to the face during the regular-season finale against the New York Liberty.

With 5.6 seconds remaining in the second quarter, Reese was defending Sabrina Ionescu when the Liberty guard’s arm caught her in the face. The officials initially called an offensive foul on Ionescu, but a replay review upgraded the ruling to a Flagrant 1.

Reese immediately headed to the locker room for evaluation, leaving teammates and fans wondering whether the injury could affect her ahead of the playoffs. She eventually returned to the court to take the two free throws awarded on the play before heading back to the locker room.

However, the situation wasn’t as serious as it may have initially appeared.

Atlanta head coach Karl Smesko offered a reassuring update after the Dream completed an 83-65 victory over New York. According to Smesko , Reese had been medically cleared to return to action. The coaching staff simply decided that there was little reason to put her back on the floor with the postseason approaching.

Reese was cleared, but Atlanta chose caution

“She was cleared, but we made a decision that it would be smart for her to sit out the second half,” Smesko said after the game.

Reese wasn’t on the bench when the third quarter began, as she remained in the locker room for the opening minutes. She eventually returned to the bench with 6:19 remaining in the period and watched the remainder of the game from the sideline.

Before leaving, Reese had recorded six points and six rebounds in 17 minutes. Atlanta, meanwhile, had built a 41-26 halftime advantage and managed to maintain control without its star forward.

The victory was particularly important for the Dream because it secured the No. 4 seed and home-court advantage in the opening round of the playoffs. Atlanta finished the regular season 31-13, while New York ended the campaign as the No. 8 seed.

The victory also marks an important milestone for Reese . She’ll enter the postseason for the first time in her WNBA career after missing the playoffs during her two seasons with the Chicago Sky.

Her 2026 campaign has been among the most productive of her young career. Reese averaged 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds per game while adding 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals. She also recorded 32 double-doubles during the regular season.

With the Dream now preparing for the playoffs, Reese’s health will naturally be a major storyline. The fact that she was cleared to return provides some reassurance, while Smesko’s decision to keep her out shows that Atlanta wasn’t willing to take an unnecessary chance in a game that no longer required Reese to play.

Now, the focus shifts toward making sure Reese’s ready when Atlanta begins its postseason run.

articles.standfirst: Indiana’s loss to Minnesota was already a tough blow, but the Fever left the court with a bigger concern: the health of two key players before the playoffs.
articles.summary: Indiana’s loss to Minnesota was already a tough blow, but the Fever left the court with a bigger concern: the health of two key players before the playoffs.
articles.body:
The loss to the Minnesota Lynx was practically sealed from the opening minutes, but the biggest concern for the Indiana Fever was not the scoreboard—it was the physical condition of their roster heading into the start of the postseason.

With the game already an uphill battle and Caitlin Clark trying to keep the team’s offense afloat, the only priority for Indiana fans was to get through the night without setbacks and arrive in the best possible shape for their debut next Sunday. Instead, the night turned into a nightmare.

The first alarm sounded with Aliyah Boston , Clark’s main partner in the paint. The center left the floor with just under three minutes remaining in the first half, did not return after halftime, and was later ruled out for the rest of the game with a lower-leg issue. Although Boston had already dealt with similar problems during the year, the Fever preferred not to risk her with the playoffs in mind, even as her actual availability remains unclear.

But the definitive blow to the team’s morale came with Ty Harris . In the third quarter, the point guard went down hard after suffering a severe-looking injury to her left leg while attempting a layup.

Harris remained on the floor for several minutes in obvious pain before being helped off to the locker room—a gut-wrenching image that set off every alarm on the Indiana bench just days before the most important stretch of the season.

How do these injuries affect Caitlin Clark’s playoff scheme?

Ty Harris’s absence drastically alters the coaching staff’s plans. Harris had established herself as a fundamental piece in Indiana’s rotation, serving as the primary backup ball-handler behind Caitlin Clark. Averaging 13.7 minutes per game, her presence allowed Clark to take key rest periods without the team’s playmaking and offensive rhythm collapsing.

If her absence is confirmed for the postseason, the minutes and responsibility on Clark’s shoulders will increase significantly, forcing her to shoulder an even heavier workload in the most demanding stage of the year.

This situation would open the door for rookie Raven Johnson, who began the season with rotation minutes before seeing her role diminish. The good news for Indiana is that Johnson knows what it means to play under maximum pressure, having starred for four years under Dawn Staley at South Carolina .

Even so, losing Harris and having Boston’s status in doubt represents a major setback for a Fever team that had managed to stay relatively healthy for most of the regular season. Indiana will await the final medical reports hoping to get both key pieces back, knowing that their chances of making a deep playoff run will depend largely on the supporting cast that can back up Caitlin Clark on the floor.

articles.title: A’ja Wilson trucked a woman with full force leaving her flat on the floor
articles.standfirst: A’ja Wilson’s strength was on full display before she even stepped onto the court
articles.summary: A’ja Wilson’s strength was on full display before she even stepped onto the court
articles.body:
There is no doubt that A’ja Wilson is one of the most dominant forces in the WNBA. It is no surprise she is considered the GOAT by many, having become the first player in WNBA or NBA history to win the scoring title, league MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and Finals MVP all in a single season.

Wilson represents elite basketball in every sense . When it comes to physical strength, she is widely regarded as one of the most powerful and resilient forces in professional basketball. That strength was on full display when she collided with a woman who was caught in the wrong place at the wrong time, sending her straight to the floor.

Wilson’s strength was impossible to miss

The moment came as Wilson walked out of the locker room with the attitude needed to go out and win a game . As she made her way through, she ran into a woman with full force and knocking her down.

Getting taken down by the strength of a professional athlete is certainly no small hit , especially when that athlete is regarded as the GOAT of the sport. Wilson made sure the woman was okay after the collision and the unexpected blow she took.

Then Wilson took over against Phoenix

The same attitude Wilson carried out of the locker room was on full display once the game against the Phoenix Mercury began . She delivered a masterclass on the court, finishing with 34 points, 10 rebounds and five assists while shooting 16-of-28 from the field in 35 minutes.

Wilson’s performance helped her team secure a 100-82 victory over the Mercury, adding another dominant night to her already impressive WNBA resume.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's worst side emerges just before playoffs, raising worst-case fears for Indiana Fever
articles.standfirst: Indiana’s 20-point loss to Minnesota dropped the Fever to sixth
articles.summary: Indiana’s 20-point loss to Minnesota dropped the Fever to sixth
articles.body:
Indiana had spent much of the final week building momentum for the WNBA playoffs. By halftime Thursday, almost all of it was gone.

The Fever were blown out 86-66 by the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in their regular-season finale, falling to the No.6 seed and setting up a first-round series against A’ja Wilson and the defending champion Las Vegas Aces .

Caitlin Clark endured the worst scoring night of her WNBA career, finishing with two points on 1-of-12 shooting in just 18 minutes. She missed all seven of her 3-point attempts and added four rebounds, three assists and a steal.

Minnesota had already built a 62-32 halftime lead, effectively ending the game as a contest and prompting Indiana to scale back minutes in the second half.

Clark misses history as Fever offense disappears

The timing made Clark ’s struggles even more striking. She entered the game 11 points short of becoming the first player in WNBA history to reach 900 points and 300 assists in a single season.

Instead, she finished well short of the milestone after Indiana’s offense stalled against Minnesota.

The performance was a sharp reversal from Tuesday, when the Fever beat the Lynx 96-77 and briefly appeared to be gathering real momentum heading into the postseason. Indiana did still get one record-breaking moment.

Kelsey Mitchell hit her 135th 3-pointer of the season, moving past Rhyne Howard ’s previous single-season mark of 134. Mitchell led the Fever with 10 points, though her remarkable streak of 20-point games ended at 27.

Washington win pushes Indiana down to sixth

The playoff consequences became clear once the Washington Mystics beat the Chicago Sky 101-93. That left Washington and Indiana tied at 28-16, but the Mystics owned the tiebreaker after winning the season series 2-1.

Washington therefore moved into the No.5 seed and will face Atlanta , while Indiana dropped to sixth and drew Las Vegas . That's a far tougher opening assignment than the Fever might have expected entering the final week.

The loss itself may not be Indiana’s biggest problem. Starting center Aliyah Boston was ruled out in the third quarter with a right lower-leg injury, while guard Ty Harris had to be carried off the court after suffering an apparent leg injury.

Indiana hadn't provided full details on either injury immediately after the game, leaving both players’ playoff status uncertain. The Fever now head into Sunday’s postseason opener trying to regroup from their worst loss of the season while preparing for Wilson and a Las Vegas team defending its title.

Clark ’s off night was dramatic, but the larger concern is what comes next. Indiana’s season is still alive. Its margin for error just got much smaller.

articles.title: Update on injuries to Aliyah Boston and Ty Harris: Stephanie White raises concerns in Indiana
articles.standfirst: Both players exited the loss to Minnesota
articles.summary: Both players exited the loss to Minnesota
articles.body:
Indiana’s regular-season finale quickly turned from a bad night into a worrying one. The Fever were already being overwhelmed by Minnesota when Aliyah Boston left late in the first half with another issue in her right lower leg.

Ty Harris then went down awkwardly in the third quarter and had to be helped from the floor, leaving Indiana with more questions than answers just days before its first-round playoff series against Las Vegas.

After the 86-66 loss, coach Stephanie White offered a more encouraging update on Boston .

“Just a flare-up, same lower leg,” White said. Asked whether Boston was kept out after halftime mainly out of caution, White answered: “Yes.”

Boston has dealt with the same lower-leg problem at different points this season, and Indiana clearly had little reason to push her once the game had slipped away.

Boston’s status looms large

Boston finished with four points and three rebounds before exiting.

Her availability is especially important because Indiana’s offense has been built around the balance created by Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Boston .

Any limitation on Boston would leave the Fever with less interior scoring and rebounding against an Aces team led by A’ja Wilson .

The timing is awkward, but White ’s description suggested Indiana may have avoided a major setback. The same reassurance wasn't available with Harris .

Ty Harris injury remains bigger unknown

Harris was hurt after an awkward landing while attacking the basket in the third quarter and needed assistance leaving the floor. White said the team was still waiting for more information.

“No update on Ty yet,” she said. “She’s still being evaluated, so hopefully we’ll have an update later.”

Asked whether Harris ’ ankle had become trapped underneath her on the play, White said she couldn't tell: “I don’t know. It was an awkward fall. I’m not really sure.”

Harris ended the night with four points and two assists.

Finale cannot follow into the playoffs

Indiana ’s problems extended well beyond the injuries. The Fever opened 2-of-16 from the field, fell behind 25-4 and finished with season lows in both field-goal percentage and 3-point shooting.

“I know I said this two games ago, but I don’t believe we shoot it like that very often,” White said. “We just need to not let that affect us on the other end. We have to continue to be better.”

Clark struck a similar tone afterward. “At this point, everybody’s record is 0-0,” she said. “We’re going into the playoffs.”

She added: “We came out and got punched in the mouth, we didn’t make shots and had two players go down. This was a pretty crappy night overall.”

Indiana now turns to a best-of-three series with third-seeded Las Vegas. The immediate priority is to get clarity on Harris and make sure Boston ’s flare-up stays exactly that.

articles.title: WNBA Playoffs 2026: Bracket, Schedule and how to watch the first round of games
articles.standfirst: Eight teams remain as the postseason begins Sunday with four first round games
articles.summary: Eight teams remain as the postseason begins Sunday with four first round games
articles.body:
The WNBA ’s 30th season has reached its elimination stage, and the final night of the regular season delivered a bracket loaded with immediate intrigue.

Minnesota finished 33-11 to secure the No.1 seed, while Golden State claimed second at 32-12. Defending champion Las Vegas landed third, Atlanta fourth, Washington fifth and Indiana sixth, with Dallas and New York completing the eight-team field.

The first round begins Sunday, September 27, and uses a best-of-three 1-1-1 format. Higher seeds host Games 1 and 3, if necessary, while the lower seed hosts Game 2.

WNBA Playoffs 2026 first-round bracket

The opening-round matchups are:

No.1 Minnesota Lynx vs. No.8 New York Liberty

No.2 Golden State Valkyries vs. No.7 Dallas Wings

No.3 Las Vegas Aces vs. No.6 Indiana Fever

No.4 Atlanta Dream vs. No.5 Washington Mystics

Minnesota-New York immediately reunites two franchises that met in the 2024 Finals, while Golden State ’s second season continues with home-court advantage against a Dallas team that completed a remarkable turnaround.

Dallas finished 27-17 after winning only 10 games the previous season, setting a WNBA record for the largest single-season improvement.

Las Vegas-Indiana may attract much of the early attention, with the reigning champions opening against Caitlin Clark and a Fever team that slipped to sixth on the final day.

First-round schedule and how to watch

All four Game 1s will be played Sunday, September 27 . The WNBA has announced two ABC windows at 2 p.m. ET and 4 p.m. ET, along with one game on Prime Video and another at 9 p.m. ET on USA Network.

The league’s official postseason schedule hasn't been assigned every matchup to its specific television window.

Game 2s will follow on Tuesday, September 29 and Wednesday, September 30 across USA Network, Prime Video and ESPN.

Any deciding Game 3s are scheduled for Thursday, October 1 and Friday, October 2 , with coverage split between ESPN, ESPN2, USA Network and Prime Video.

What happens after the first round?

The semifinals begin Sunday, October 4 and expand to a best-of-five 2-2-1 format.

The WNBA Finals start October 17 and remain best-of-seven, with a potential Game 7 scheduled for October 31.

After 44 regular-season games, expansion storylines and a late scramble for positioning, the path to the championship is finally clear.

Eight teams remain, and the margin for error is immediately small, so lose twice in the opening round, and the season is over.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark sends a stern warning to her Indiana Fever teammates regarding the playoffs following the latest disaster
articles.standfirst: Clark urges Indiana to forget the loss and turn its attention toward the postseason
articles.summary: Clark urges Indiana to forget the loss and turn its attention toward the postseason
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever couldn't have asked for a worse way to close out the regular season. Minnesota dominated from the opening minutes, racing ahead 25-4 before eventually handing Indiana an 86-66 defeat.

The loss was the Fever's biggest of the season and came with two significant injury scares involving Aliyah Boston and Tyasha Harris.

Caitlin Clark also endured a night she'd rather forget. The Fever guard scored just two points on 1-of-12 shooting, including an 0-for-7 showing from three-point range. It was the lowest-scoring game of her WNBA career.

However, Clark wasn't interested in allowing the disastrous performance to define Indiana's postseason outlook.

“I feel like at this point everybody’s record is zero and zero. We’re going into the playoffs. If we sit and sulk about what happened tonight, yeah, it sucks,” said Clark .

“It is what it is. We kind of came out and got punched in the mouth. We didn’t make shots. Obviously, we had two players go down. This was a pretty crappy night overall.”

Clark wants Fever focused on the playoffs

“If you can’t get up for the playoffs, then you probably shouldn’t be on this team,” Clark said after the game, emphasizing the importance of buying into the group and fighting for the people around them.

The message comes at a crucial moment for Indiana. Boston left the game in the second quarter with a flare-up of a lower-leg issue and didn't return. Harris then suffered a left ankle injury in the third quarter and had to be carried from the floor. The Fever have yet to determine the full extent of either injury.

Those developments could make Indiana's playoff challenge even more complicated. Boston remains an important presence in the frontcourt, while Harris provides depth behind Clark in the backcourt. Losing either player would create another obstacle for a team that's already dealt with considerable roster disruption.

Indiana's shooting was another major problem against Minnesota. The Fever finished with only 66 points and shot 34% from the field. Kelsey Mitchell managed just 10 points, ending her remarkable streak of 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points.

The defeat dropped Indiana to the No. 6 seed, meaning the Fever will face the Las Vegas Aces in the opening round. A win against Minnesota would've moved Indiana into fifth place and sent the team to Atlanta instead.

Now, the regular season is over and the stakes are completely different. Clark knows Thursday's performance wasn't good enough, but rather than focusing on it, she's demanding that the Fever respond when the games matter most.

articles.standfirst: Golden State and Indiana reached the playoffs through very different paths.
articles.summary: Golden State and Indiana reached the playoffs through very different paths.
articles.body:
The regular season is over, and it left behind an image that is difficult to ignore. Golden State Valkyries finished second in the WNBA, while Indiana Fever, with Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston among its main stars, finished sixth.

The difference was not only in the standings. Both teams reached the playoffs after building very different seasons, and the contrast between their paths helps explain why Golden State managed to finish so high.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham just gave fans a reason to compare her to Stephen Curry
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham went from playing just seven minutes in one game to delivering a key performance, just as her three-point numbers put her back in the spotlight.
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham went from playing just seven minutes in one game to delivering a key performance, just as her three-point numbers put her back in the spotlight.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham went from having an important role in the Indiana Fever rotation to barely seeing the floor in one game. The decision drew criticism, but it also raised a more interesting question: just how good has her three-point shooting really been this season?

From 20 minutes to just seven

The drop in her playing time was obvious. On September 18, Cunningham played 20 minutes against Toronto , but two days later, against the Washington Mystics, she spent just seven minutes on the court .

Stephanie White explained that the decision was related to Cunningham’s effort on defense and on the boards.

Sophie Cunningham decided to look in the mirror

After that game, Cunningham spoke about her responsibility within the team and what she could do differently.

“I had to look in the mirror: What can I do better?” she said.

The answer came on the court. Against Minnesota, Cunningham played 29 minutes again, scored 11 points, knocked down three of her six three-point attempts and finished with a +17 . She also reached 2,000 career points.

The turnaround was obvious, but the stat that eventually put her name alongside Steph Curry came from somewhere else: her podcast, No Hesitation .

The stat that put her next to Steph Curry

During the episode, her co-host pointed out that Cunningham was shooting 42.7% from three, while Curry owns a 42.4% career three-point percentage .

There is an important distinction to the comparison: it does not mean Cunningham is a better shooter than Curry, because it compares what Sophie is doing in 2026 with Steph’s career average. But that is exactly what makes the number interesting: this season, Cunningham is shooting above the mark Curry has built over the course of his career .

Her co-host also brought up Steph to put those nights when the shots simply do not fall into perspective. He noted that even Curry has finished games without making a three and has had hundreds of games below percentages that would normally seem unthinkable for one of the greatest shooters in basketball history.

And perhaps that is the most interesting part of the comparison. Cunningham does not need a perfect night for her season to speak for itself. That 42.7% shows what she is doing when you look at the bigger picture.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell power the Fever to the greatest offensive season in WNBA history ahead of the playoffs
articles.standfirst: This season, Clark finished third in points per game with 22.3, and Mitchell finished second with 24.7
articles.summary: This season, Clark finished third in points per game with 22.3, and Mitchell finished second with 24.7
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever did not finish the regular season the way they would have preferred , dropping an 86-66 decision to the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in their final tune-up to secure the sixth seed in the WNBA standings.

For Fever MVP candidates Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell , this particular contest is one to erase immediately from memory as they pivot their complete focus toward an upcoming first-round playoff series against the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces , the very same squad that eliminated Indiana in a grueling semifinal battle last season.

Clark endured a rare off-night, finishing with a career-low 2 points while shooting 1-of-12 from the field and 0-of-7 from beyond the arc . Meanwhile, Mitchell chipped in 10 points , bringing a dramatic halt to her incredible streak of 27 consecutive games scoring 20+ points , cementing a WNBA record that will likely stand for quite some time.

Even with that sour finale, their collective regular-season output was transcendent, propelling the Fever to a league-record 96.0 points per game and an all-time high of 4,222 total points scored across the entire campaign.

Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell Cement MVP-Caliber Individual Seasons

On an individual level, the historic numbers put up by Clark and Mitchell firmly validate their status among the elite.

Clark concluded the year ranking third in scoring with 22.3 PPG and second in assists with 8.3 APG , becoming the first player in league history to finish in the top three in both categories while generating a record 41.2 combined points and assists per game , the most offensively productive season the association has ever witnessed.

She amassed 891 total points , setting the single-season scoring record for a guard, while becoming the first player ever to record 800+ points and 300+ assists in a single year, alongside logging her second season with 100+ three-pointers and 300+ assists .

Furthermore, Clark notched 10 games with 25+ points and 10+ assists (more than any player has accumulated in an entire career) and 13 games with 20+ points and 10+ assists (no other player has even reached 10 in a career).

Mitchell's MVP resume proved equally stellar, as she finished second in the league in scoring (24.7 PPG) while breaking the single-season record with 1,086 total points . She also shattered the single-season mark for three-pointers made (135) and recorded 35 total games with 20+ points , anchoring her record-setting 27-game streak .

If the Fever intend to make noise in October, bouncing back from their regular-season finale slump is non-negotiable.

Fever Chase Championship Glory in Rematch With Las Vegas Aces

Despite increasing their win total for the third consecutive year, jumping from 20 wins in 2024 and 24 wins in 2025 to 28 victories in 2026, the Fever finished sixth in the standings for the third straight season.

Now, Indiana prepares for a high-stakes postseason rematch against the Las Vegas Aces. Unlike last year's heartbreaking Game 5 semifinal overtime defeat , the Fever will have Caitlin Clark healthy and ready on the floor.

Ever since Clark arrived as the No. 1 overall draft pick in 2024 , the franchise has steadily climbed the postseason ladder, exiting in the first round as rookies before reaching the semifinals a year ago.

The ultimate objective is clear: reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2015 and capture the franchise's second championship banner (its only prior title coming in 2012 ).

To accomplish that mission, Indiana must first conquer the Aces, outlast the winner of the Wings-Valkyries series, and ultimately battle through the grueling opposite bracket featuring powerhouse teams like the Lynx, Liberty, Dream, and Mystics.

articles.title: Controversy is brewing: ESPN reminds Caitlin Clark that she isn't the best in the WNBA just yet
articles.standfirst: The Fever star finished behind A’ja Wilson in the postseason rankings, sparking debate from both supporters and critics
articles.summary: The Fever star finished behind A’ja Wilson in the postseason rankings, sparking debate from both supporters and critics
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark enters the WNBA Playoffs after the most productive regular season of her career, but ESPN 's latest player rankings have ensured the conversation around her is not limited to basketball.

The Indiana Fever guard was ranked No. 2 among players competing in the postseason, behind Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson and the decision proved immediately controversial, with some fans arguing about where Clark should place.

The ranking of Clark quickly became bigger than the overall ranking itself and reaction on social media was predictably split as fans took to X.com, formerly known as Twitter, to react.

One user wrote, “That’s a joke.”

Another second said, “Nasty work. ESPN has fell off.”

And a third commented, “Is this a joke in the last game she was missing.”

That tension reflects the unusual place Clark occupies in the league. Her 2026 numbers were elite at 22.3 points, 8.3 assists and 4.0 rebounds per game, but almost every assessment of her now becomes part of a larger argument about her status.

ESPN ’s Kareem Copeland highlighted the scale of her season, writing that Clark “finished the best year of her career ranked No. 3 in points” and was “at the helm of the league’s No. 1 offense.”

But the disagreement is notable because it is coming from opposite directions as some fans believe Clark ’s scoring and playmaking should have placed her ahead of the Aces ’ Wilson .

Others point to Wilson ’s MVP credentials and complete two-way impact as the reason ESPN got the top spot right whilst Clark 's Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell was ranked No. 5 entering the postseason.

Caitlin Clark’s impressive 2026 WNBA season

Clark ’s finale should not obscure the season she had, although her final regular-season game was easily one of her worst as she scored two points on 1-of-12 shooting in Indiana’s 86-66 loss to the Minnesota Lynx .

But that came after a stretch in which she averaged 30.2 points and 10.0 assists over five games whilst she also finished the year third in the WNBA in scoring and second in assists, while recording 14 points-assists double-doubles.

One of the clearest examples of her ceiling came in July, when she produced 45 points and 10 assists in a single game. That adds to the stakes of the ranking because Clark and Wilson are about to face each other.

Indiana enters the playoffs as the No. 6 seed and opens against No. 3 Las Vegas , giving the first round a direct matchup between the two players ESPN placed at the top of its list.

The Aces eliminated the Fever in last season’s semifinals, though Clark did not take part in that postseason after an injury-shortened year. This time she is healthy and coming off a career-best regular season.

Heading straight into a series against the player ranked above her, can the 24-year-old prove she deserved the nod ahead of Wilson ? Even if she does, the online argument over ESPN ’s order is unlikely to disappear.

articles.title: Angel Reese turns her offseason trade into a breakout campaign emerging as a favorite for a major WNBA honor
articles.standfirst: Reese finished as the leading rebounder for the third consecutive season, the same number of seasons she has spent in the WNBA
articles.summary: Reese finished as the leading rebounder for the third consecutive season, the same number of seasons she has spent in the WNBA
articles.body:
Weeks before the 30th WNBA season began, the Atlanta Dream shocked the basketball world by acquiring Angel Reese from the Chicago Sky in exchange for their 2027 and 2028 first-round draft picks .

Fast forward to the postseason, and that blockbuster gamble has paid massive dividends: Atlanta secured the fourth seed in the standings to set up a first-round series against the Washington Mystics , while Chicago languished with a losing record for the fourth straight year.

For Reese, this marks her maiden playoff appearance, though her regular-season dominance entirely justified Atlanta's aggressive trade.

She captured the league's rebound title (12.2 RPG) for the third consecutive year , matching the exact length of her professional career, and cemented her readiness for playoff intensity by earning Player of the Week honors for three consecutive weeks after closing out the campaign averaging 19.3 points and 9.0 rebounds in the last week of action

Angel Reese Chases DPOY Crown Behind Record-Breaking Campaing

With the 30th regular-season schedule officially in the books, the major individual awards are coming into sharp focus: Olivia Miles is locked in as the runaway Rookie of the Year , A'ja Wilson is poised to secure her fifth career MVP award , and the most fiercely contested race centers on the Defensive Player of the Year (DPOY), where Reese stands as the betting favorite across major sportsbooks.

Reese faces stiff competition from Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams and multi-time MVP Wilson, but her resume is undeniably robust.

Alongside leading the association in rebounding ( 12.1 RPG ), she finished third in steals ( 1.8 SPG ) while anchoring advanced metrics by ranking first in defensive win shares and fourth in defensive rating, earning her recognition as The Athletic’s Defensive Player of the Year.

Reese concluded the campaign averaging 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds , appearing in 43 of Atlanta's 44 games, and permanently etching her name into the WNBA history books by shattering the single-season record with 32 double-doubles . She officially surpassed Alyssa Thomas' previous benchmark of 28 double-doubles set across 40 games in 2023.

Furthermore, the former LSU national champion broke additional league records this year by hauling in the most total rebounds in a single season (521) and grabbing a jaw-dropping 26 rebounds in a single game .

The Dream will now open their playoff run with Game 1 at home tomorrow at 7:00 PM ET, followed by Game 2 on Wednesday in Washington, and a decisive Game 3, if necessary, back in Atlanta next Friday.
